name: Dext
summary: Receipt and invoice capture that extracts the data and feeds it into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage. It is the capture layer, not accounting software, so you still need one of those.
best_for: accountants, bookkeepers and growing businesses drowning in receipts who want fast, accurate capture flowing straight into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage
skip_if: you're a sole trader with few receipts (pricey for low volume), or you want all-in-one accounting — Dext only does the capture layer
honest_knock: It's a data-capture layer, not accounting software — it feeds Xero, QuickBooks or Sage, so you still need one of those. Extraction accuracy varies and sometimes needs manual fixes, the UI is tricky for beginners, the mobile app is more limited than desktop, and sole traders find it pricey. In our own test on 21 October 2026, on two clean made-up receipts, every field we checked was right; a rotated copy of one was flagged as a duplicate but still counted against the 250-document allowance, and a byte-identical copy vanished without a message.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month billed annually for 250 documents and 5 users ($31.50 billed monthly), excluding tax
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-10, read in a browser on dext.com/en/business/pricing because the price panel renders client-side) Dext has moved off named tiers: you choose a region and a billing period, then slide an allowance. The base of 250 documents a month and 5 users costs $25.21 per month billed annually ($302.50 a year) or $31.50 monthly in the Rest of the World, £30 monthly in the UK, €31.50 in the EU and A$42 in APAC, all excluding tax. The annual discount is stated as up to 20% everywhere except the UK page, which says up to 19%. Add-ons are billed separately: AI Assist $10.5 a month until 31 January 2027 (the page said 31 October when we read it on 21 August 2026), Commerce Lite from $7.50 and Vault free for 100MB then from $4. Line Item Extraction and Supplier Statement Extraction are from $20.50 a month or $0.50 per document, and Bank Statement Extraction from $13.00 a month or $0.32 per document. Plans include 10 sheets of bank statement extraction, 5 line-item documents and 5 supplier statement extractions as free credits, and the free trial is 14 days with no payment details required.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 during the 14-day trial, without a card and without connecting accounting software or a bank: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We uploaded two made-up receipts whose every field we knew, then a byte-identical copy of one and a rotated copy of the other.
findings: Both receipts reached the Costs inbox within about a minute, and all eight fields we checked were right: date, supplier, total and tax on each (EUR 12.10 with EUR 2.10 tax, and EUR 21.80 with EUR 1.80 tax). Dext picked the category itself: 'Office Supplies' for the stationery receipt and 'Travel' for the transport one.
The rotated copy was marked 'Duplicate' in Submission history and kept out of the inbox, which is right, but it still counted: the usage counter went from 0 to 3 of 250 for two receipts.
The byte-identical copy appeared nowhere, not even in Submission history: it was dropped without a message.

The workspace worked straight away without any connection. Onboarding asked three questions (industry, company size and accounting software, with Spreadsheets as an option); the overview showed 'Documents extracted 0 / 250, Resets in 1 days' and trial credits for 10 bank statement, 5 supplier statement and 5 line-item extractions, 5 Vault AI credits and 500 MB of Vault storage.

Upload offers one document per file (PDF, JPG, PNG, ZIP), one per page (PDF) or auto-splitting (PDF, 'Can take up to 1 hour'), with limits of 6 MB per image or PDF, 100 MB per ZIP and 40 MB for an auto-split PDF. Each account also gets its own email address for sending in documents.

Net amount and tax rate in the detail view
Real, creased or handwritten receipts, and other currencies
Publishing to accounting software, a bank connection and the mobile app
What happens after the trial, and what the 250 per period means exactly
